correctness.rationale: At height z the slice is sT with s=1−(1−t)z, hence for t<1 its volume-induced scale distribution is proportional to s² on [t,1]. Conditional on scale the dimensionless base coordinates (U/(bd),Y′=V/b) are independent of scale, with Y′ density (r+1−y)/(r+1/2) and E[U/(bd)|Y′=y]=(r+1−y)/2. Thus base cross-covariance in these coordinates is −Var(Y′)/2; E[Y′]=(r/2+1/6)/(r+1/2) and E[Y′²]=(r/3+1/12)/(r+1/2) give the claimed ρ. Scaling gives Cov(X,Y)=E[S²]Cov(U,V)+Var(S)E[U]E[V]. The positive prefactor leaves q−ρ with q=1−15(1−t⁴)²/[16(1−t³)(1−t⁵)] for t<1. Cancellation gives the finite endpoint values q(0)=1/16 and q(1)=0 and the displayed strictly negative derivative for 0<t<1; the prism also directly has the negative base covariance. The sign of q(0)−ρ is that of the given cubic; one sign change and opposite endpoint signs give its single positive root. Strictly decreasing ρ gives increasing t*, with t*→0 as r↓r* and t*→1 as r→∞; matching q(t)∼(1−t)²/12 to ρ(r)∼1/(6r) gives the stated √2 limit. A fresh bounded numerical check from the slice moments also agreed with the root and both signed witness moments. The supplied checker was inspected, not executed; its finite tetrahedral tests use floating hull triangulation with rational moment integration and are supplementary. The positive-to-negative orientation is for increasing t (widening the top); the phase diagram itself gives the direction unambiguously.

value.rationale: In this canonical nonrectangular coordinate family the negative base cross-covariance competes with a positive common-scale fluctuation. The theorem tells a user exactly whether taper can reverse it, gives the unique taper at which the moment vanishes when reversal is possible, and quantifies the thin transition scale at large aspect. This complete sign diagnostic for a natural interpolation between prism and pyramid is more useful than computing a moment for an isolated shape and makes no affine-invariant or general-prismatoid claim.
